html:
The women wholesale traders of the Grand Marche of Lome who, from the 1960s to the 1980s, controlled the trade in wax-print cloth for much of West and Central Africa.

They bought Dutch wax prints, above all from Vlisco, gave patterns their popular names and sold them on to traders from across the region. They grew rich enough to drive Mercedes-Benz cars, which gave them their name, and they backed and funded Eyadema's regime. The devaluation of the CFA franc in 1994, political unrest and cheap Chinese copies ended their dominance. They remain a symbol of African women's power in market trade.
sum: The women wholesale traders of the Grand Marche of Lome who, from the 1960s to the 1980s, controlled the trade in wax-print cloth for much of West and Central Africa.
